suspicions.claim: Self-follow attempt returns 400 instead of 409 when user already follows themselves (impossible state)
suspicions.trigger: 1. Create user A. 2. Manually insert a self-follow row in followers table (follower_id=A.id, followed_id=A.id). 3. Authenticate as A. 4. POST /api/me/following/A.id. 5. Observe 400 response (new check) instead of 409 (existing is_following check).
suspicions.evidence: probe_s1 POST /api/me/following/1 returned 204 on base and 400 on head, showing the new self-follow check returns 400 instead of creating a follow (204) or returning 409 for existing follow.

suspicions.claim: Self-follow attempt returns 400 with generic error message instead of specific "User already followed" message
suspicions.trigger: 1. Authenticate as any user. 2. POST /api/me/following/<own_id>. 3. Read response body: code=400, message="Bad Request" (generic) instead of code=409, message="Conflict" with description about already following.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s2 POST /api/me/following/2 returned 204 on base and 400 with generic 'Bad Request' message on head, confirming self-follow returns 400 with generic error instead of 409 with specific conflict message.

suspicions.claim: Self-follow attempt returns 400 before checking if target user exists, leaking existence of user IDs
suspicions.trigger: 1. Authenticate as user A (id=1). 2. POST /api/me/following/999 (non-existent). 3. Observe 404 (user not found). 4. POST /api/me/following/1 (self). 5. Observe 400 (self-follow rejected). The different status codes reveal that user 1 exists while 999 does not.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s3 POST /api/me/following/999 returned 404 on both, but POST /api/me/following/1 returned 204 on base and 400 on head, showing different status codes (404 vs 400) reveal user existence.

suspicions.claim: Self-follow attempt returns 400 instead of 404 when DISABLE_AUTH=true and default user (id=1) follows themselves
suspicions.trigger: 1. Set DISABLE_AUTH=true. 2. Ensure user id=1 exists. 3. POST /api/me/following/1 (no auth header). 4. Observe 400 response. Before PR this would create a self-follow (204) or return 409 if already following.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s4 POST /api/me/following/1 with DISABLE_AUTH returned 204 on base and 400 on head, confirming self-follow returns 400 instead of 204 or 409 when auth is disabled.

suspicions.claim: Self-follow attempt bypasses is_following check, changing behavior for duplicate follow attempts
suspicions.trigger: 1. Authenticate as user A. 2. POST /api/me/following/A.id (first attempt) -> 400. 3. Manually insert self-follow row in DB. 4. POST /api/me/following/A.id again -> 400 (new check) instead of 409 (is_following check). The second attempt now returns 400 instead of 409.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s5 POST /api/me/following/3 returned 409 on both base and head for duplicate follow attempts, showing the is_following check still returns 409 and is not bypassed.
